definitions.explanation: Describing someone or something that relies excessively on another person, substance, or system. Often carries a negative connotation suggesting unhealthy dependence.

examples.japanese: {依存的|いそんてき}な{関係|かんけい}は{良|よ}くない。
examples.english: A dependent relationship is not healthy.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{親|おや}に{対|たい}して{依存的|いそんてき}な{態度|たいど}を{取|と}りがちだ。
examples.english: He tends to have a dependent attitude toward his parents.

examples.japanese: スマートフォンに{依存的|いそんてき}になりすぎると、{日常生活|にちじょうせいかつ}に{支障|ししょう}が{出|で}ることがある。
examples.english: If you become too dependent on your smartphone, it can interfere with daily life.

notes:
Formed from {依存|いそん} (dependence) plus the adjectival suffix {的|てき}. Primarily used in psychology, relationships, and social commentary. Almost always carries a negative connotation — healthy reliance is usually expressed differently.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {依存的|いそんてき}な{関係|かんけい}: dependent relationship
- {依存的|いそんてき}な{性格|せいかく}: dependent personality
- {依存的|いそんてき}な{態度|たいど}: dependent attitude
- {依存的|いそんてき}になる: to become dependent

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {依存|いそん}する: to depend on — the verb form; more neutral than {依存的|いそんてき}
- {甘|あま}えた: spoiled; clingy — describes dependency in a more emotional, interpersonal way
- {自立|じりつ}した: independent; self-reliant — the antonym

PRONUNCIATION NOTE:
The reading いそん is now standard, though the older pronunciation いぞん is still heard.
